instruction.text: Find and select Europe on the map.

feedback.end: Throughout the 1800s, it was very popular to go on tours around Europe. Young, rich men went to improve their knowledge of art, languages and culture.

instruction.text: You are speaking with Sebastian, who is on a Grand Tour of Europe. Fill in the gaps.

atoms.b: Hello Sebastian! How are you finding your ((++tour floor)) of Europe?
atoms.sound: ssml:<prosody pitch='-0.5st'>Hello Sebastian! How are you finding your tour of Europe?</prosody>

atoms.b: I have seen many beautiful places! I am also collecting lots of books and works of ((++art food)) to take home with me.
Do you have anyone ((++travelling dancing)) with you?
atoms.sound: ssml:<prosody pitch='-0.5st'>Do you have anyone travelling with you?</prosody>

atoms.b: My tutor is here with me. He is helping to ((++educate exercise)) me about each place that we visit.
Where do you plan to ((++go read)) next on your tour?
atoms.sound: ssml:<prosody pitch='-0.5st'>Where do you plan to go next on your tour?</prosody>

atoms.b: Our final destination is Rome, but we are first spending a few months in Florence. I cannot wait to see ((++Italy space))!

instruction.text: Draw a line between Florence and Rome to complete Sebastian’s tour.

atoms.a: How do you think Sebastian would have travelled?

feedback.finish: The building of railway networks during the 1800s increased the popularity of Grand Tours. Many wealthy families viewed them as an essential part of their children’s education.

instruction.text: Drag the old coins to the correct place on the image.

feedback.end: It was common for travellers on tours of Europe to collect souvenirs and send them back home. These objects included coins, paintings, books and ancient pottery.
